reading: The auto-VERDICT DECAYS_BUT_OFF_PREDICTED_RATE was fooled by averaging in the s=40 numerical break. Correct reading from the clean prefix s=10->20->30: alpha-alpha_min decays exponentially at 0.321/0.318 digits/s, matching the predicted zero-temperature rate 0.348 (set by |rho2|/|rho1|=0.449). So the golden-edge gap is the LIMIT NOT YET REACHED (item i, math), NOT a numerical floor -- the 7.2 digits at s=25 was simply s=25 not being infinity; at s=30 it is 9.73 digits, on the predicted line. SEPARATELY, item (ii) the numerical floor sets in at s>=40 even at dps=95: the Perron filter is not perfectly robust when the true eigenvalue phi^{-2s} nears the eigenvector noise (s=40 grossly failed while s=50 partly recovered -- a filter-selection wart, not a monotone resolution wall). Trustworthy edge range at these settings: s<=30. This does not touch the multifractal curve (max s=25) and both items of the reviewer dichotomy are now separated by regime.
